Simulation of an assembly process from a multilayer meta-web: C++ core

Source: R/RcppExports.R
metaWebNetAssemblyMLCT.Rd

Low level simulation used by metaWebNetAssemblyML(). Most users should call metaWebNetAssemblyML(), which takes the network as layers and the effects as the parameters beta; this function takes instead the three matrices built from them by build_multilayer_assembly(). Use it directly to run many simulations of the same network without rebuilding the matrices.

Usage

metaWebNetAssemblyMLCT(metaW, M, Dep, m, e, se, time)

Arguments

metaW

Logical trophic adjacency matrix of the meta-web, metaW[j, i] is TRUE if j is a prey of i.

M

Numeric matrix, M[i, j] is the effect of the presence of j on the log extinction rate of i (the diagonal is ignored).

Dep

Logical matrix, Dep[i, j] is TRUE if i depends obligately on j.

m

A numeric vector of species' migration rates from the meta-web

e

A numeric vector of species' baseline extinction rates

se

A numeric vector of species' secondary extinction rates (no prey, or no obligate partner)

time

Simulated time, the state is recorded at integer times 1 to time-1

Value

A list as metaWebNetAssemblyCT(): S and L (number of species with trophic links and of trophic links at each time), STime (species presence, species x time) and A (trophic adjacency matrix of the final local web), plus rejected, the number of rejected extinction proposals.

Details

It is the continuous time model of metaWebNetAssemblyCT() with two additions:

  • Non-trophic modifiers of extinction: the extinction rate of species i depends on which species are present, \(e_i(t) = e_i \exp(\sum_j M_{ij} x_j(t))\), where \(x_j(t)\) is 1 if species j is present. M is in units of log extinction rate: build_multilayer_assembly() puts \(-\beta_+\) (divided by the number of positive partners if normalize = TRUE) where j has a positive effect on i, and \(+\beta_-\) where it has a negative one. So a negative \(M_{ij}\) (a mutualist, a facilitator) lowers the extinction rate of i while j is present and a positive one (a competitor) raises it. With M = 0 the model is metaWebNetAssemblyCT().

  • Obligate dependence: if species i depends on at least one species (Dep[i, ] has a TRUE) and none of them is present, i goes extinct with the secondary extinction rate se, as a predator without prey does.

The state dependent extinction rate is simulated exactly by thinning: extinction events are proposed with the upper bound \(e_i \exp(\sum_j \max(M_{ij},0))\) and accepted with probability \(e_i(t)\) divided by that bound. Large positive values in M make the bound large and the simulation slower (more rejected proposals).

See also

metaWebNetAssemblyML(), build_multilayer_assembly(), metaWebNetAssemblyCT()
